title: Cottage Pie
subtitle: Beef mince and vegetables under a mash crust
excerpt: A deeply savoury beef mince filling with carrots, celery, and herbs under a thick layer of golden mashed potato. This is the kind of dish that improves overnight, making it ideal for cooking ahead.
sourceNotes: Cottage pie appeared in British recipe books as early as 1791, originally as a way to use up leftover roast meat. The modern version with fresh beef mince became standard in the 20th century and is now one of Britain's most recognised comfort dishes.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cool completely, cover the dish, and freeze for up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat at 180 C for 30 to 35 minutes until piping hot throughout.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the filling and freeze in batches. Top with fresh mash when ready to bake.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the filling up to 2 days ahead and refrigerate. Top with mash and bake on the day.

content.text: Let the filling simmer long enough to reduce and concentrate. A watery filling will make the mash topping slide and the pie will not hold when served.

Heat a large pan over high heat. Brown the beef mince in batches without stirring until well coloured. Remove and set aside. Reduce the heat to medium, add the onion, carrot, and celery with a splash of oil. Cook for 8 to 10 minutes until soft.

Stir in the garlic and tomato puree. Cook for 2 minutes. Return the browned mince to the pan. Add the Worcestershire sauce, beef stock, thyme, and bay leaves. Bring to a simmer, then cook uncovered for 25 to 30 minutes until the filling is thick and the liquid is mostly absorbed. Remove the bay leaves and season well.
While the filling cooks, boil the potatoes in salted water for 18 to 20 minutes until tender. Drain well, return to the pan, and mash with the butter and warm milk. Season generously.
Preheat the oven to 200 C. Transfer the filling to the roasting tin and spread the mash over the top. Use a fork to create a rough textured surface so it crisps up well.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the topping is golden and the filling is bubbling at the sides. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

items.cause: Not simmered long enough to reduce
items.fix: Keep the lid off and simmer until the sauce is thick and coats the mince.

items.cause: Filling was too hot when mash was added
items.fix: Cool the filling slightly before adding the mash.

items.cause: Covered for too long in the oven
items.fix: Add a splash of stock to the filling before reheating and cover loosely.
